subject: Hosted API commit overspend — proposed remedy flow and required docs
messages:
From: Greg Morris <greg.morris@saasops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@saasops.com>, SaaSOps Billing <billing@saasops.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected overage vs committed tier — Q3 usage attached

Hi Camila,

We just closed out Q3 usage and saw a sizeable overage relative to our committed tier. I attached our exported usage for the quarter; the overage is primarily driven by two spikes in September from an ad-hoc batch of log ingestion and a campaign burst.

Can you outline what remedy options Redwood offers for hosted API commits? Specifically:
- How do make-good credits work for quarterly true-ups vs annual reconciliations?
- Can we get a provisional credit while we sort the usage evidence?
- What documentation or approvals do you need from our side?

We’re reviewing next-quarter budgeting and would like a clear, short timeline so we can finalize our internal finance ask.

Thanks,
Greg Morris
Head of Platform, SaaSOps
[Attachment: SaaSOps_usage_Q3.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Greg Morris <greg.morris@saasops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage vs committed tier — Q3 usage attached

Greg — thanks for the upload and the clear summary. I reviewed the CSV quickly and can confirm the two September bursts explain the majority of the overage. Below is a pragmatic remedy flow we follow for hosted API commit overspends; happy to refine based on your preference.

Proposed remedial flow (summary):
1) Provisional relief: Redwood can issue a provisional one-off credit equal to 25% of the overage token spend while we complete reconciliation. This is conditional on a signed commit amendment or statement of work within 10 business days so Finance can book the credit.
2) Full reconciliation: At quarter close we run the official true-up comparing committed tokens vs actual. If the commit shortfall remains, make-good credit is issued per the contract make-good schedule (typically pro-rated or converted to credits applied to future invoices).
3) Alternative options: Convert the outstanding usage into a short-term reserved commit (3 months) at an adjusted tier with a back-dated effective date to cover the overspend. This is useful when customers expect sustained higher usage.
4) Documentation: We need the signed amendment (we’ll draft), your official PO/approval line for finance, and the raw usage export (you provided). For audit we may ask for campaign notes for the September burst.

Attachments: I attached a draft amendment that captures the provisional credit and the proposed 3-month commit conversion path. Please review and flag changes.

Next steps I recommend:
- Greg: confirm you want the provisional credit (yes/no)
- If yes: sign the attached amendment so we can apply the credit on the next invoice
- Ben/Naomi: please review the draft amendment for pricing and invoicing implications

I’ll hold on next-quarter invoice actions until we confirm.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: commit_amendment_draft.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Greg Morris <greg.morris@saasops.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage vs committed tier — Q3 usage attached

Adding pricing context here so expectations are aligned.

High-level: SaaSOps’ committed tier sits at the "Pro-250M" bracket (per-token). Your aggregated Q3 actual sits roughly 18% above the committed bucket, which triggers the standard overage rates. We can do the following as a one-time make-good offer to close this quickly:
- Apply a 30% credit on the incremental overage amount (not on committed volume) for Q3 only.
- If you convert the overage into a 3-month reserved commit within 7 business days, we’ll apply an additional 5% one-time discount on the converted volume and grandfather current pricing for the duration.

Rationale: provisional credit + convert-to-commit gives you immediate relief and predictable unit economics for the next quarter.

If you want the provisional credit only (no conversion), we need the signed amendment Camila shared and a PO reference for invoices. If you choose conversion, we’ll generate a short-term addendum and update the billing schedule.

I’ve added a HubSpot note with the pricing table and our recommended SKU for the converted commit here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8921

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greg Morris <greg.morris@saasops.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage vs committed tier — Q3 usage attached

Folks — quick note from Finance on mechanics and timing so expectations are clear:

1) Accounting treatment options:
   a) Apply a credit memo on the next invoice cycle: fastest operational path once we have the signed amendment and PO. Credit will appear as a line-item negative charge and will reduce the net due.
   b) One-time invoice reversal and reissue: used if the overage has already been paid and customer prefers a corrected invoice. This takes longer (2–3 billing cycles to complete).
2) Documentation required to issue credits: signed amendment (electronic signature accepted), valid PO reference from SaaSOps, and the usage export (we received).
3) Cutoff dates: To make the provisional credit effective on the Dec invoice, we need the signed amendment by EOD 2026-11-30. If we miss that, the earliest application will be the Jan invoice.
4) Audit & controls: We will keep the CSV and amendment in the customer folder and include a short memo in the accounting record.

Attaching our standard credit memo template for your legal team to review.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: credit_memo_template.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

From: Greg Morris <greg.morris@saasops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:58:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage vs committed tier — Q3 usage attached

Thanks — that all makes sense and I appreciate the clear options. We will: 
- Take the provisional credit + convert 60% of the overage to the 3-month reserved commit (Ben’s suggested SKU).
- I’ll send an internal PO to billing later today and ask our legal to review the amendment.

Please send the DocuSign for the amendment and I’ll route it for signature. If we can hit the 11/30 amend cutoff for the Dec invoice that would be ideal.

Greg
Greg Morris
Head of Platform, SaaSOps
